name: Marketing
description: The marketing concept, mix, research, consumer behaviour, product, price, promotion, distribution and e-marketing, aligned to the WAEC Marketing syllabus and related Commerce/JAMB topics.

topics.name: Introduction to Marketing
topics.summary: What marketing is, how it differs from selling, and the ideas that guide a marketing-oriented firm.

subtopics.name: Meaning and Functions
subtopics.summary: Marketing as identifying, anticipating and satisfying customer needs profitably.

objectives.text: Define marketing and distinguish it from selling and from advertising
State the functions of marketing
Explain why every organisation, including a school or a church, markets

subtopics.name: Marketing Concepts
subtopics.summary: Production, product, selling, marketing and societal-marketing orientations.

objectives.text: Describe the production, product, selling, marketing and societal concepts
Give a Nigerian example of a firm that still behaves as if 'a good product sells itself'
Explain why the marketing concept puts the customer first

subtopics.name: The Marketing Mix
subtopics.summary: The 4Ps, and the extra 3Ps used for services.

objectives.text: Name the 4Ps and state the role of each
Add people, process and physical evidence for a service
Show how the mix must be consistent for a given target market

topics.name: Markets and the Consumer
topics.summary: Who the customer is, how markets are split, and why people buy.

subtopics.name: Markets and Segmentation
subtopics.summary: Consumer, industrial and organisational markets, and how a firm carves out a segment.

objectives.text: Distinguish consumer from industrial and organisational markets
Define market segmentation, targeting and positioning
Segment a market by geography, demography, psychography and behaviour

subtopics.name: Consumer Behaviour
subtopics.summary: The buyer-decision process and the factors that shape it.

objectives.text: Outline the consumer decision-making process
Explain cultural, social, personal and psychological influences on buying
Distinguish a high-involvement from a low-involvement purchase

subtopics.name: Organisational Buying
subtopics.summary: How firms and government departments buy, and why it differs from household buying.

objectives.text: State features of organisational buying
Name the buying roles in a decision-making unit
Contrast a new-task buy with a modified or straight rebuy

topics.name: Product
topics.summary: What the firm offers: levels of a product, classification, mix and life cycle.

subtopics.name: Product Levels and Types
subtopics.summary: Core, actual and augmented product, and convenience, shopping and speciality goods.

objectives.text: Explain the core, actual and augmented levels of a product
Classify consumer goods as convenience, shopping or speciality
Distinguish a product from a service

subtopics.name: Product Mix and Branding
subtopics.summary: Width, length and depth of the mix, and why brands matter.

objectives.text: Define product mix, line, width, length and depth
State the functions of branding, packaging and labelling
Give Nigerian examples of a family brand and of individual branding

subtopics.name: The Product Life Cycle
subtopics.summary: Introduction, growth, maturity and decline, and the marketing decisions at each stage.

objectives.text: Sketch and label the product life cycle
State typical marketing actions at each stage
Explain why a firm extends a product's life

topics.name: Price
topics.summary: How a price is set, and the tactics used to move it.

subtopics.name: Pricing Objectives and Methods
subtopics.summary: Cost-plus, break-even, going-rate and perceived-value pricing.

objectives.text: State common pricing objectives (profit, market share, survival, image)
Calculate a cost-plus price from unit cost and a mark-up
Compare cost-plus, break-even, competition-based and value-based pricing

subtopics.name: Pricing Tactics
subtopics.summary: Penetration, skimming, discounts, psychological pricing and price discrimination.

objectives.text: Distinguish market-skimming from market-penetration pricing
Explain cash, trade and quantity discounts
Give an example of psychological pricing and of price discrimination

subtopics.name: Responding to Price Changes
subtopics.summary: What a firm does when a competitor cuts price, or costs rise.

objectives.text: List options when a competitor reduces price
Explain why a firm might hold price when costs rise
Discuss the risks of a price war

topics.name: Promotion
topics.summary: The promotional mix: advertising, sales promotion, public relations, personal selling and direct marketing.

subtopics.name: The Promotional Mix
subtopics.summary: The five tools and when each is the right one.

objectives.text: Name the elements of the promotional mix
State factors that influence the mix (budget, product type, stage of the life cycle)
Distinguish above-the-line from below-the-line promotion

subtopics.name: Advertising and Sales Promotion
subtopics.summary: Paid media versus short-term incentives to buy.

objectives.text: Define advertising and state its types and media in Nigeria
Define sales promotion and give examples (coupons, samples, bonuses, merchandising)
State merits and demerits of advertising

subtopics.name: Public Relations and Personal Selling
subtopics.summary: Earned reputation, and the salesperson's role.

objectives.text: Define public relations and give tools (press release, sponsorship, events)
State the steps in the personal-selling process
Compare personal selling with advertising for an industrial product

topics.name: Place and Distribution
topics.summary: How the product reaches the customer, and who stands in between.

subtopics.name: Channels of Distribution
subtopics.summary: Zero-, one- and two-level channels, and why middlemen exist.

objectives.text: Define a channel of distribution and draw common channel diagrams
State the functions of middlemen
Choose a suitable channel for a given product

subtopics.name: Retailing and Wholesaling
subtopics.summary: The last two links, seen from a marketer's point of view.

objectives.text: State the marketing functions of retailers and wholesalers
Explain intensive, selective and exclusive distribution
Discuss the growth of supermarkets and online retail in Nigeria

subtopics.name: Physical Distribution
subtopics.summary: Order processing, warehousing, inventory and transport — the logistics of place.

objectives.text: List the components of physical distribution
Explain the trade-off between inventory cost and customer service
State factors that influence the choice of transport

topics.name: Research and the Marketing Environment
topics.summary: Finding out before deciding, and the forces a marketer cannot control.

subtopics.name: Marketing Research
subtopics.summary: The research process, and primary versus secondary data.

objectives.text: Define marketing research and state its uses
Outline the research process from problem definition to report
Distinguish primary from secondary data, and qualitative from quantitative methods

subtopics.name: The Marketing Environment
subtopics.summary: Micro and macro forces that shape marketing decisions in Nigeria.

objectives.text: Distinguish the micro-environment from the macro-environment
List PESTEL forces with a Nigerian example of each
Explain how a firm responds to an uncontrollable environmental change

subtopics.name: Marketing Information Systems
subtopics.summary: The standing system that feeds managers, not just one-off research.

objectives.text: Define a marketing information system
Name its components: internal records, intelligence, research and analysis
Explain why a small Nigerian firm still needs information even without a research department

topics.name: Further Marketing
topics.summary: Services, e-marketing and the sales force — the later topics on the WAEC paper.

subtopics.name: Services Marketing
subtopics.summary: Intangibility, inseparability, variability, perishability, and the extra 3Ps.

objectives.text: State the distinctive characteristics of a service
Explain how a bank or an airline uses people, process and physical evidence
Give examples of service quality from a customer's point of view

subtopics.name: E-marketing
subtopics.summary: Websites, social media, search and mobile as marketing channels in Nigeria.

objectives.text: Define e-marketing and list its tools
State advantages and limitations of marketing online in Nigeria
Outline ethical issues: privacy, false claims and unsolicited messages

subtopics.name: Sales Management
subtopics.summary: Recruiting, training, motivating and controlling a sales force.

objectives.text: State the functions of sales management
Explain how a sales force can be organised (by product, territory or customer)
Describe common methods of remunerating salespeople
